reporting-org.narrative: Defence for Children International Netherlands - ECPAT Netherlands

description.narrative: Sexual exploitation of children (SEC) is a grave violation of children’s rights and affects millions of children and youth annually, regardless of gender. No region, country or child is immune, though girls, boys and children with other gender identities face differing levels of risk to different manifestations of SEC depending on their intersectional vulnerability factors. It impacts heavily and long lastingly on their physical, emotional and mental well-being. It deprives children and youth of establishing healthy (sexual) relationships and from developing to the best of their potential. The SUFASEC programme is designed to combat SEC and will work in 12 countries in Latin America and South and South East Asia: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Guatemala, India, Indonesia, Laos, Nepal, Philippines and Thailand.

The SUFASEC programme is designed to combat SEC by working towards the following long-term impact: “Children in all of their diversity are better protected from sexual exploitation.” This activity forms part of the SUFASEC programme. The long-term impact will be reached through three interlinking objectives that address different dimensions (social norms, assets/environments, and laws/policies/systems). 1. Children, youth and their communities successfully challenge social norms and harmful practices related to SEC 2. Children and youth have access to and are supported by strengthened assets and protective environments 3. Children and civil society meaningfully participate in holding duty bearers, including government and local authorities, accountable to their obligations towards improved (implementation of) laws, policies, and systems

The different stakeholder groups involved in the SUFASEC programme include:- Children and youth in all their diversity: A child-centred approach: children and youth are the most important stakeholders. When children/youth fall victim to SEC the physical and mental impact can be long lasting. The Alliance adheres to the UN definition of child (0-18 years) and youth (15-24 years)- Caregivers and Communities: Critical stakeholders in the community include parents, caregivers, community leaders, teachers, local Community Based Organisations (CBOs), social workers, and other community members involved in community based child protection mechanisms.- CSOs and CBOs: Local child protection organisations support and implement activities at community level, L&A towards national actors, and provide synergies of interventions.- Local and national governments: formulate, endorse and implement laws and public policies related to SEC- Private Sector: Travel and tourism orgs (e.g., large and small, hotels, transport), as well as ICT/ Digital Service Providers have interest to avoid SEC taking place within their value chain, and to avoid having their products and services used to facilitate SEC- International donors, Intergovernmental bodies, INGOs, Multilateral entities55: Targeted audiences and partners for evidence based regional and international lobbying- Dutch Stakeholders: NL Embassies in programme countries, MoFA, MoJ&S, to formalise the network for sustainable cooperation to end SEC and impunity of offenders. The Dutch Public- Media & Journalists: Investigative and reporting outlets in the Programme countries. Media and journalists in the Netherlands.

title.narrative: Greater and safer access to quality child protection and local SRHR information and services

comment.narrative: The child protection servises are also included in this indiactor. In Cedeca Bahia, which operates at the local level in the Project., the data involving sexual violence is alarming in the country. Since 2006, 2023 was the year that recorded the most complaints involving cases of sexual exploitation on the internet. In relation to sexual abuse there was an increase of 70% compared to the previous year. Bahia is one of the states with the highest record of violence, historically remaining in this position on the national scene.

Psychosocial counselling for children and adolescents who have been victims of sexual violence, offering ongoing therapeutic counselling. Age range: 03 to 17 years old of both sexes, with a variety of gender identities and sexual orientations. The counselling involves processes of accountability and comprehensive counselling by the family and the state, especially in cases involving children with no family reference or whose ties have been broken by court order. The action includes institutional visits, home visits and case discussions within the network, as well as various referrals.

Esta ação acontece em nível local, através do Centro de Defesa da Criança e do Adolescente Yves de Roussan - Cedeca Bahia, e traz como ação estratégica o gerenciamento de até 30 casos envolvendo violências sexuais. A metodologia do trabalhado do Cedeca se dá com base na Lei nº 8.069/1990 - Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescentes, através da Política de proteção jurídico-social e do serviço de prevenção e atendimento psicossocial (art. 87, V e III). A equipe garante além do acompanhamento terapêutico, o encaminhamento e acompanhamento de demandas sociais e jurídicas, bem como atenção a integralidade que envolve a garantia da proteção dessas crianças e adolescentes, não somente na sede do Cedeca, mas nos demais equipamentos da rede que compõe o Sistema de Garantia de Direitos.

Bahia has historically held the main positions in the registration of sexual violence against children and adolescents in Brazil. There is a great deficiency in the care policies for these victims, and the absence of equipment to care for these victims and their families is diagnosed. The management of 30 cases, through the work of Cedeca Bahia, will make it possible to relieve services and guarantee psychosocial and legal assistance to children, adolescents and their families, ensuring reception, care and referral, articulating sectoral and intersectoral policies.

This action takes place at the local level, through the Child and Adolescent Defense Center Yves de Roussan - Cedeca Bahia, and it involves the strategic management of 30 cases involving sexual violence. Cedeca's work methodology is based on Law No. 8,069/1990 - the Statute of Children and Adolescents, through the legal-social protection policy and psychosocial prevention and care services (Article 87, V and III). In the first year of the project the cases were and are under follow-up, involving victims of sexual violence, associated with other rights violations. The team ensures, in addition to therapeutic support, the referral and follow-up of social and legal demands, as well as attention to the comprehensiveness that involves guaranteeing the protection of these children and adolescents, not only at Cedeca's headquarters, but also in other network facilities that make up the Rights Guarantee System, namely: Social Assistance Reference Center - CRAS, Specialized Reference Center for Social Assistance - CREAS, Public Defender's Office, Public Prosecutor's Office, Women's Hospital, Child and Adolescent Psychosocial Care Center - CAPS IA, Guardianship Council, and Trans Ambulatory - Center for Studies and Therapy of Drug Abuse - CETAD/BA, and civil society organizations such as ACOPAMEC, OAF, Pearls of Christ (which execute institutional care services for children and adolescents in partnership with the municipality).

title.narrative: Children and youth access comprehensive correct SRHR and SEC information
# of young people (male) reached with comprehensive, correct information on sexuality, HIV/AIDS, STIs, pregnancy and contraception

comment.narrative: This indicator include young people reached with information on SEC (and not only SRH). In Cedeca Bahia, which operates at the local level in the Project, there is a huge lack in prevention work with children and adolescents, and the fragility with regard to training on the topics that involve sexual and reproductive rights and sexual violence is notorious, being a desire of the organizations that work with this public in spaces like these. The fragility is linked both to difficulties in handling the theme and to the moralistic and distorted idea that talking about these issues is hurting rights and not the other way around.

The training sessions are scheduled to take place in two places: schools and civil society organisations that work directly with children and adolescents in contexts of sexual violence and other violations. The collective involves children and adolescents aged between 6 and 17, of different gender identities, who are methodologically separated according to their age group. The whole process involves a welcoming space, the definition of demands (based on previous work with organisations on the public's profile) and dialogic and fluid methodologies, applied according to each group. The use of audiovisual strategies also fulfils the methodological rite.

02 grupos participaram dos ciclos formativos: crianças e adolescentes em acolhimento institucional, que buscou aprofundar os temas sobre sexualidade, direitos sexuais e reprodutivos e autoproteção., em especial por serem crianças em contextos de violências sexuais e em um projeto social em um bairro periférico de Salvador, onde observou-se maior interesse dos adolescentes no diálogo sobre direitos sexuais, quebra de tabus e dúvidas sobre possibilidades de autoproteção de cenários de IST (infecção sexualmente transmissível) e gravidez na adolescência. O coletivo entendeu como importante aprofundar o tema sobre a violência sexual, em especial no contexto da escola e da internet.

The training cycles will target children and adolescents from 8 to 17 years old, with an expected reach of 100 people. Its training path will be to work with the theme of sexual and reproductive rights, and cross-cutting themes, such as gender, sexuality and prevention against sexual violence in its multiple forms. It will be carried out in institutions that already work with the public, also seeking to add training for educators and families.

In the first year of the project, two training circuits were carried out through the local action of Cedeca Bahia, one in partnership with the Pierre Verger Foundation and the other with the Sementinha Project, reaching a total of 66 children and adolescents.For the children's group (from 6 to 11 years old), they were able to talk openly about their bodies and understanding the biological aspects such as being able to correctly name sexual organs and how this is considered a protective measure. Girls were given a particular attention as to when being educated on menstruation. For adolescents (from 12 to 17 years old), SRH was raised through a dialogue strategy that allowed them to share doubts and experiences. Pregnancy was the most observed topic. In both groups the possibiity to continue within the training spaces was offered, which would also allow for the training of parents, mothers and educators.
